intro: Step in: one click, and the whole desktop looks like another era - colours, fonts, corners, shadows, even Snake. The programs stay the same. Only a few dozen variables change.
arrived: Arrived: {era}. The whole desktop looks like this now - open a program and see for yourself.
backHome: Back in the present: Amonel OS.

era1946.name: ENIAC
era1946.look: Lamps and switch panels: amber on black, no screen.

era1956.name: Mainframe
era1956.look: Paper from the teletype, typewriter type.

era1971.name: UNIX
era1971.look: Green phosphor, scanlines, a blinking cursor.

era1984.name: Macintosh
era1984.look: Black on white, 1 bit deep, a pixel font.

destination.title: Enter a year
destination.explain: Enter any year from 1946 on - the machine lands in the era whose look was current then.
destination.label: Year
destination.tooEarly: {year, number, ::group-off}? This machine does not go back that far: this site's journey begins in 1946 with ENIAC.
destination.future: {year, number, ::group-off} has not been built yet. The machine only travels into the past.

storage: This browser remembers your choice under "amonel.theme.v1" until you return to the present. It never leaves your device.
truth: A theme is only data: the same programs, other values for colour, type and shape. That is exactly how today's interfaces keep content and look apart.
